system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (**AUD 4.8m**). | 25% of price (**AUD 6m**); 20% only with Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Reject; counter at 25% (AUD 6m)**—no approval for the conditional fallback has been given. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, but only the excess is recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 aggregate tipping basket; once exceeded, recover from the first dollar. | **Reject; counter at playbook thresholds**—the Seller’s thresholds are materially higher and its basket is deductible, not tipping. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; proposes limits apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | 24 months for general claims; keep separate regimes for other claim types. | **Reject; counter at 24 months**—18 months needs Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate regime: 100% cap and at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; require the separate regime**—Seller’s “administrative simplicity” would collapse protections the playbook reserves for title and capacity. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; this is non-waivable. | **Reject; insist on the carve-out**—the Seller’s all-Claims formulation cannot override the playbook’s non-waivable position. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records; also makes specific disclosures. | Specific fair disclosure; reject deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters found by prudent search. | **Reject general deemed disclosure; retain specific fair disclosures**—the Seller’s broad language sweeps in unparticularised material. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | **Reject; delete the blanket bar**—deemed or adviser knowledge must not extinguish claims, particularly protected categories. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; treats consent as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure letter says final consent and evidence of conditions being satisfied are absent. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. | **Reject; make both evidence of effective consent and satisfied conditions a Completion requirement**—consent-on-delivery is insufficient and the current disclosure confirms the gap. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms it is unpaid and no final security discharge is included. | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. | **Reject deferred release; require payout and effective releases at Completion**—the disclosed facility remains outstanding and no approved exception is identified. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are Seller’s matter and not separately itemised in the funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them. | **Require a specific funds-flow line or Seller funding, including applicable on-costs**—the disclosed amounts are absent from the draft flow and on-costs remain unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 makes transfer conditional on all SOW3 fees being cleared; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open but is not independent payment verification, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. | Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified either way. | **Seek a broader indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure**—the transfer condition and missing payment/assignment evidence leave risk beyond the narrow payment-only protection. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material. DD-006 says access, scope and notification status are undetermined; no loss amount is stated. | Preserve logs, investigate and provide updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Require preservation, investigation and updates without assuming an outcome**—the disclosure is preliminary and supports neither a confirmed breach nor a conclusion of immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are characterised as ordinary-course costs. Disclosure says whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course is not established. | Assess the renewals; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate and assess; do not automatically classify as Debt or deduct the price**—the disclosed records do not resolve their nature or treatment. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says limitations and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance terms apply to all Claims and considers Tax/IP settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate, with no hidden general-regime override. | **Reject the blanket override; preserve distinct regimes and leave Tax/IP open**—Seller’s all-Claims language would blur protections and does not settle open terms. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller as holder of 100%; no independent evidence is offered. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | **Require independent verification**—a register recording the Seller as holder does not independently establish the full title position. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax/IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms open; do not assume unlimited liability or resolution. | **Do not accept the claimed settlement; continue negotiating Tax/IP terms separately**—no buyer authority or verified agreement in the materials resolves these open terms. |

The Seller’s “STANDARD,” “accepted,” “agreed” and “settled” labels are counterparty assertions, not buyer authority or evidence of agreement.
=== END ADVICE ===
